DILG Republic of the Philippines DEPARTMENT OF THE INTERIOR AND LOCAL GOVERNMENT DILG-NAPOLCOM Center, EDSA comer Quezon Avenue, West Triangle, Quezon City http://www.dilq.com.ph DILG OPINION NO. 50 s.2020 June 19, 2020 HON. JOSEPH A. RANOLA Office of the Municipal Mayor Municipality of Jagna Province of Bohol Dear Mayor Rafiola: This has reference to your letter dated 30 April 2020 requesting for the Department's legal opinion on the following: i. Can Vice-Mayor Theodore R. Abrenilla who was stranded due to COVID-19 be declared on absent without official leave (AWOL)? ii. Can Vice-Mayor Abrenilla preside the regular Sangguniang Bayan session through virtual session? iii. Can Vice-Mayor Abrenilla practice his medical profession outside of his territorial jurisdiction? Per your letter, the Vice-Mayor of Jagna, Bohol, Dr. Theodore R. Abrenilla is physically absent in the Municipality of Jagna since 15 March 2020 up to the date Of your letter as he was stranded in Cebu due to the enforcement of no sail policy. Hence, the above-mentioned queries. Foremost, Section 46 of Republic Act (RA) No. 7160, otherwise known as the Local Government Code of 1991 (LGC) states that there exist a temporary vacancy when the local chief executive is temporarily incapacitated to perform his duties for physical or legal reasons, such as, but not limited to: (1) leave of absence; (2) travel abroad; and (3) suspension from office. The absence of Vice- Mayor Abrenilla is attributed to legal reasons due to the no sail policy imposed, in compliance with the directives to contain the spread of the COVID-19. Nevertheless, because of the lack of specific provisions in the LGC in dealing with temporary vacancies in local elective offices, particularly in the local sanggunians, DILG Memorandum Circular No. 2019-21 was issued to remedy the same. Where, it is provided that there is a temporary vacancy in the office of the vice-governor or city or municipal vice mayor if he/she is temporarily incapacitated to perform his/her duties for physical or legal reasons such as, but not limited to, leave of absence, travel abroad, and suspension from office. Hence, when a temporary vacancy exists in the office of the provincial vice governor or city or

municipal vice mayor, the highest ranking sangguniang panlalawigan/ panlungsod/bayan member, as the case may be, shall be designated by the President, through the SILG or the OIC-DILG immediately upon the report of the concerned DILG Regional Office of the said vacancy, as acting provincial vice governor or city or municipal vice mayor. Accordingly, this Department is of the view that Vice-Mayor Abrenilla cannot be charged with AWOL, rather, a temporary vacancy existed. In reply to the second query, again, there is no law, rules and regulations, even RA 11469 or the Bayanihan to Heal as One Act which was passed primarily to address the Covid-19 pandemic and the Presidential decrees issued by the Office of the President, which authorize the local sanggunians to conduct sessions through teleconferencing, video conferencing and other electronic means. Due to the absence of any law, rules and regulations, the following provisions of the LGC still govern the conduct of sanggunian sessions, to wit: SECTION 52. Sessions. - (a) On the first day of the session immediately following the election of its members, the Sanggunian shall, by resolution, fix the day, time, and place of its regular sessions. The minimum number of regular sessions shall be once a week for the Sangguniang Panlalawjgan, Sangguniang Panlungsod, and Sangguniang bayan, and twice a month for the Sangguniang Barangay. (b) When public interest so demands, special sessions may be called by the local chief executive or by a majority of the members of the Sanggunian. (c) All Sanggunian sessions shall be open to the public unless a closed-door session is ordered by an affirmative vote of a majority of the members present, theæ-h.eing-a-quarum, in the public interest or for reasons of security, decency, or morality. No two (2) sessions, regular or special, may be held in a single day. (d) In the case of special sessions of the Sanggunian, a written notice to the members shall be served personally at the member's usual place of residence at least twenty- four (24) hours before the special session is held. Unless otherwise concurred in by two-thirds (2/3) vote of the Sanggunian members present, there being a guqrum, no other matters may be considered at a special session except those stated in the notice. (e) Each Sanggunian shall keep a journal and record of its proceedings which may be published upon resolution of the Sanggunian concerned. SECTION 53. Quorum. - (a) A majority of all the members of the Sanggunian who have been elected and qualified shall constitute a quorum to transact official business. Should a question of quorum be raised during a session, the presiding officer shall immediately proceed to call the roll of the members and thereafter announce the results. (b) Where there is no quorum, the presiding officer may declare a recess until such time as a quorum is constituted, or a majority of the members present may adjourn from day to day and may compel the immediate n 1

designating a meméer Qf the Sanggunian, to be assisted member or members pf the police force assigned in the territorial jurisdiction Of the gQvernment unit concerned, to arrest the absent member and present him at the sessiqn. (c) If there is still no quorum despite the enforcement of the immediately preceding subsection, no business shall be transacted. The presiding officer, upon proper motion duly approved by the members present, shall then declare the session adjourned for lack of quorum. (Emphasis Supplied) While there is also no categorical statement in the aforequoted provisions of the Code requiring the physical presence of the sanggunian members to conduct a session, such physical presence can be inferred therefrom. On the last query on whether or not Vice-Mayor Abrenilla can practice his medical profession outside of his territorial jurisdiction, Section 90 of the LGC categorically provides that: "SECTION 90. Practice of Profession. - (a) All governors, city and municipal mayors are prohibited from practicing their profession or engaging in any occupation other than the exercise of their functions as local chief executives. b) Sanggunian members may practice their professions, engage in any occupation, or teach in schools except during session hours: Provided, That Sanggunian members who are also members of the Bar shall not: (1) Appear as counsel before any court in any civil case wherein a local government unit or any office, agency, or instrumentality of the government is the adverse party; (2) Appear as counsel in any criminal case wherein an officer or employee of the national or local government is accused of an offense committed in relation to his office. (3) Collect any fee for their appearance in administrative proceedings involving the local government unit of which he is an official; and (4) Use property and personnel of the government except when the Sanggunian member concerned is defending the interest of the government. (c) Doctors of medicine may practice their profession even during official hours of work only on occasions of emergency: Provided, That the officials concerned do not derive monetary compensation therefrom. "

It is clear from the foregoing that only the I-CES are prohibited from practicing their profession or engaging in any occupation other than the exercise of their functions as LCEs. We hope we have addressed your concern accordingly. Very truly yours, By Authority of the Secretary: MARIVEL C. SACENDONCILLO, CESO 111 Undersec etary for Local Government Dir. Leocadio T. Trovela Regional Director, DILG-Region VII Sudlon, Lahug, Cebu City Ls/90
